Hi Hiroshi — great to hear from you. Quick note on the regional offsets so we avoid the "next-day" trap: on the dates you suggested Sydney is observing AEDT (UTC+11), Tokyo is JST (UTC+9), and Singapore is SGT (UTC+8). That means Sydney is 3 hours ahead of Singapore and 2 hours ahead of Tokyo.

Proposed 45-minute windows (all times shown in local zones):
- Option A: 09:30 SGT / 10:30 JST / 12:30 AEDT (good for execs after morning ops)
- Option B: 13:00 SGT / 14:00 JST / 16:00 AEDT (after lunch for SG/JPN, late afternoon SYD)

If either works I will send a single invite with the Zoom link and an attached agenda. Marcus will demo the latency/cost dashboard and Mina will cover dedicated/private deployment controls.

Also: when we send the .ics, we'll make sure the event start time uses the recipient's local TZ so calendars don't display it as "next day" for Sydney. Some client calendars (older Exchange setups) still interpret ICS DTSTART without explicit TZ tags — we'll include both TZ and UTC timestamps to be safe.

Which option do you prefer?

Best,
Olga Petrov
Enterprise AE — Redwood Inference

Hi Olga — thanks for the clear options. I think Option A (09:30 SGT) is better for our Tokyo team, but one point of confusion: when I said "late morning Tokyo" I meant their local late morning (10:30 JST), which maps to 12:30 in Sydney the same day — that's fine.

However, our Sydney ops lead noted that when he accepts invites in Outlook the event shows up as 12:30 *the previous day* (weird), so he asked whether you can explicitly set the event time in the invite to both local time and UTC (e.g., DTSTART;TZID=Australia/Sydney:20261125T123000 and DTSTART:20261125T013000Z). That should avoid parsing differences across clients.

Also, can you confirm the day (we meant Thu, Nov 25 local) — sometimes "Nov 25" in Sydney is still Nov 24 in US view.

Apologies for the extra detail — we just want to avoid calendar churn.

Best,
Hiroshi
